payload.title: Building a tcgen05 GEMM from Scratch: Reaching 98% of cuBLAS on Blackwell
payload.summary: A step-by-step implementation of a Blackwell matrix multiplication kernel using raw PTX tcgen05 instructions, progressing from a basic kernel to 98% of cuBLAS performance through swizzling, pipelining, warp specialization, 2-SM MMA, and persistent kernel techniques.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.gist: `tcgen05` is a set of PTX instructions for programming Tensor Cores on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (SM100, not to be confused with consumer Blackwell SM120).

sections.heading: 2. High-Performance Matrix Multiplication Review
sections.gist: Matrix multiplication of A (shape MxK) and B (shape KxN) produces output C of shape MxN.

sections.heading: 3. Basic tcgen05 Kernel
sections.gist: The Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA), available since Hopper, issues memory loads with minimal register usage and address computation.

sections.heading: 4. 128-Byte Global Loads and Swizzling
sections.gist: Swizzling avoids shared memory bank conflicts by distributing data across all 32 banks.

sections.heading: 5. Pipelining
sections.gist: Standard N-stage pipelining: maintain N in-flight global→shared load stages, each with its own shared memory buffer.

sections.heading: 6. Warp Specialization
sections.gist: Since only 1 thread issues TMA and 1 thread issues MMA, dedicate separate warps to each task.

sections.heading: 7. 2-SM MMA
sections.gist: Blackwell allows two CTAs to cooperatively compute a single MMA tile.

sections.heading: 8. Persistent Kernel with Static Scheduling
sections.gist: In-kernel profiling reveals that epilogue and per-tile setup consume significant time, leaving Tensor Cores idle.

sections.heading: 9. Performance Summary
sections.gist: table columns: Kernel, TFLOPS, % of cuBLAS

sections.heading: 10. Observations
sections.gist: Tensor Core programming on Blackwell feels easier than previous generations due to dedicated hardware and instructions.
